questions.question: If it was Tuesday on 22 July 1969, then what will be the day of the week on 6 August 1985?
questions.solution:
Given: 22 July 1969 is Tuesday.

Now, 1969 to 1985 = 16 Years.

In 16 years, 4 Leap year and 12 ordinary years.

Total odd days from 22 July 1969 to 22 July 1985 = (4 × 2) + (12 × 1) = 8 + 12 = 20 days.

And, 20 days = 20/7 = 2 week and 6 odd days.

So, 22 July 1985 was = Tuesday + 6 = Monday.

Now, 22 July 1985 to 6 August 1985 = 15 days, 15/7 = 2week and 1 odd day.

Therefore, 6 August 1985 = Monday + 1 = Tuesday.

Hence, the correct option is "Option 1".

__
 
• The** first wave of the Green Revolution **package was received by more prosperous states of Haryana, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Western Uttar Pradesh.
 
• 
 
The Green Revolution in India:

 
 
• The Green Revolution, which refers to the large-scale introduction of high-yielding varieties of seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides in agriculture, has been criticized for its negative impact on small farmers.
 
• The Government of India launched the Green Revolution in 1965 under the Third Five-Year Plan(1961-66).
 
• MS Swaminathan is considered the father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• Norman Borlaug is known as the 'Father of Green Revolution' in the world.
 
• In India, the aim of this revolution was to increase the productivity of agricultural crops, particularly wheat and rice.
 
 
• The main focused crops were Wheat, Rice, Jowar, Bajra and Maize.
 
 
 
• In the first phase of the Green Revolution, the use of HYV seeds was limited to the more prosperous states of Haryana, Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Western Uttar Pradesh.
 
• HYV seeds refer to high-yielding varieties of seeds that were developed during the Green Revolution to increase crop yields.
 
 
• These are resistant to insects and diseases and have a high yield capacity.​
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution was a period of agricultural transformation that took place in the 1960s and 1970s in India.
 
• The goal of the Green Revolution was to increase agricultural productivity and food security by introducing high-yielding crop varieties (HYV seeds), modern irrigation systems, and chemical fertilizers and pesticides.

questions.question: Which of these is a conventional weaker section lending under formal sector?

options.text: Self help group bank linkage model

• **Commercial banks priority sector lending (PSL)**:

 
 
• This refers to **mandatory lending requirements imposed by regulatory authorities** like the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI**) **on commercial banks**.
 
• These banks must allocate a specific portion of their **loans to specific categories considered "weaker sections," **including small and marginal farmers, micro and small enterprises, and weaker sections of society like **scheduled castes** and** scheduled tribes**.
 
• This makes it the most conventional and widespread form of formal sector lending reaching these groups.
 
• Rather of financing only successful industries or locations that are crucial to economic growth, the aim of a PSL project is to give credit to the less fortunate segments of society.
 
• Financial assistance is readily available to all key sectors, allowing them to apply for loans that banks are obligated to provide at a reduced interest rate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• While they reach some weaker sections, they are not considered formal sector lending.
 
 
 
• **Self-help group (SHG) bank linkage model**: This model connects self-help groups formed by underprivileged individuals with banks, facilitating access to formal credit.
 
• **Microfinance institutions (MFIs)**: Although MFIs cater to low-income populations, they are specialized institutions separate from the mainstream banking system.

questions.question: The net worth of any bank is equal to ___________.

• To determine a **bank's net worth**, you **subtract its liabilities from its assets**.

 
 
• i.e. Total assets minus total liabilities.
 
 
 
• Assets: Everything the bank owns (loans, cash, investments, buildings, etc.)
 
• Liabilities: Everything the bank owes (customer deposits, loans payable, etc.)
 
• Net worth: The difference between assets and liabilities (what the bank truly owns after accounting for all its debts)

questions.question: In India, ___________ fixes the CRR for the banks in the economy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) fixes the CRR for the banks in the economy.
 
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is an important tool used by the RBI to manage liquidity in the banking system and control inflation.
 
• Cash reserve ratio (CRR): 
 
 
• It is a monetary policy tool used by central banks, including the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), to regulate and control the money supply in the economy.
 
• CRR is the percentage of total deposits that commercial banks are required to keep as reserves with the central bank.
 
• It is a portion of the bank's demand and time liabilities.
 
• The primary objective of implementing CRR is to ensure the liquidity and stability of the banking system while controlling inflation and managing credit growth.
 
• When the central bank increases the CRR, it reduces the amount of money available for lending by commercial banks.
 
• This helps reduce excess liquidity in the economy by controlling inflationary pressures and curbing excessive credit expansion.
 
• On the other hand, **when **the **central bank decreases the CRR**, **it increases the amount of money available for lending by commercial banks**.
 
• This can stimulate credit growth, promote economic activity, and ease liquidity conditions in the economy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Reserve Bank of India (RBI):

 
 
• It is **India’s central bank**.
 
• In compliance with the terms of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, it was founded on April 1, 1935 in Calcutta.
 
• It was permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937.
 
• Though originally privately owned, since nationalisation in 1949, the Reserve Bank is fully owned by the Government of India.
 
• It also functions as the "lender of last resort" and is considered Banker to Banks.
 
• It regulates the issue of Bank notes and keeping of reserves with a view to securing monetary stability in India and generally to operate the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage.
 
• It also monitors the monetary policies through its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).

⇒ Time taken by Shyam (alone) to complete a work = Total work / Efficiency of Shyam

⇒ Time taken by Shyam = 36 / 1 = 36 days

**∴ The correct answer is 36 days.**
